mentions.heading: Commodity cost increases and availability of raw materials
mentions.detail: Aluminum, copper, nickel, resins, steel, energy, castings, forgings; relies on pass-through provisions and selective hedging
mentions.quote: While we seek to alleviate the impact of increasing costs by including material pass-through provisions in our customer contracts wherever possible and by selectively hedging certain commodity exposures, we may not be successful in these efforts.

mentions.heading: Falling commodity prices may cause supply interruptions
mentions.detail: Rapid commodity price falls may lead suppliers, carriers and energy providers to withdraw capacity
mentions.quote: From time to time, commodity prices may also fall rapidly. If this happens, suppliers may withdraw capacity from the market until prices improve, which may cause periodic supply interruptions.

mentions.heading: Elevated inflation increases input costs
mentions.detail: Cost-recovery agreements in 2022-2024 did not recover 100% of increased costs, hurting margins
mentions.quote: Following non-contractual negotiations, we reached cost-recovery agreements with various customers in 2024, 2023 and 2022, but these agreements did not enable us to recover 100 percent of our increased costs, and as a result, our operating margins were negatively impacted.

mentions.heading: We may not achieve the expected benefits of our restructuring plans
mentions.detail: Ongoing capacity and cost realignment; risks of labor unrest, lost key employees, unrealized savings
mentions.quote: Implementation of any restructuring action may be costly and disruptive to our business, and we may not be able to realize the cost savings, operational improvements and estimated workforce reductions that we anticipate within the projected timing or at all.

mentions.heading: Changes in trade policy, including tariffs, may have an adverse effect
mentions.detail: 2025 U.S. tariffs on EU, Canada, Mexico, China raised material costs; Chinese retaliatory tariffs; recovery from customers uncertain
mentions.quote: In 2025, the U.S. announced significant tariffs on imports from a broad range of countries, including the European Union, Canada, Mexico and China. These tariffs have increased the cost of raw materials and components we purchase
